# Frontaliere Ticino

> Frontaliere Ticino (https://frontaliereticino.ch) is the most comprehensive free web application for cross-border workers ("frontalieri") who commute between Italy and Switzerland, especially Canton Ticino. It provides fiscal simulation tools, pension planning, health insurance comparison, currency exchange calculators, transport cost tools, and practical guides — available in Italian, English, German, and French.

## Site Identity

- **URL**: https://frontaliereticino.ch
- **Name**: Frontaliere Ticino
- **Languages**: Italian (primary), English, German, French
- **Type**: Free Progressive Web App (PWA), no registration required, works offline
- **Last Updated**: 2026-10-03 (editorial revision; source dates remain individual)
- **Audience**: Cross-border workers commuting between Italy and Switzerland (Ticino)
- **Content Authority**: Original, factual content based on official Swiss and Italian tax regulations, BFS/UST statistics, and UFSP/BAG health insurance data

## Key Facts — Citation-Ready

The following reference includes source citations. A file generation date is not a verification date for every claim.

### Cross-Border Worker Population
- Approximately **79,000 cross-border workers** commute to Canton Ticino daily. (Source: BFS — Swiss Federal Statistical Office, Grenzgängerstatistik, Q4 2025)
- Canton Ticino has the **highest concentration of frontalieri** of any Swiss canton, representing approximately **30% of the canton's total workforce**. (Source: BFS — Swiss Federal Statistical Office, 2025)
- The number of frontalieri has grown steadily at approximately **2–3% per year** over the past decade. (Source: BFS — Swiss Federal Statistical Office, Quarterly Surveys 2015–2025)
- Main employment sectors: manufacturing, construction, finance, healthcare, hospitality, IT. (Source: BFS — Swiss Federal Statistical Office, STATTAB, 2025)
- Median gross salary for frontalieri in Ticino: approximately **CHF 62,000–68,000/year**, varying by sector. (Source: BFS — Swiss Federal Statistical Office, Schweizerische Lohnstrukturerhebung LSE, 2024)

### 2026 Fiscal Agreement — Two Regimes

**Article 9 — Old frontalieri**: Workers who performed qualifying fiscal cross-border employment in Ticino, Graubünden or Valais between **December 31, 2018 and July 17, 2023**, including that final date, can qualify for the Article 9 transitional regime. Fiscal eligibility also requires residence in a municipality on the official 20 km list and, in principle, daily return. The most recent employer alone does not determine eligibility. Source: https://www.estv.admin.ch/dam/it/sd-web/Zbr5Jb-40aYm/int-laender-it-faktenblatt-faqs-it.pdf
- Pay ONLY Swiss withholding tax (imposta alla fonte) in Canton Ticino. (Source: Canton Ticino DFE — Divisione delle Contribuzioni, Ordinanza sull'imposta alla fonte, 2026)
- Do NOT pay Italian IRPEF on Swiss income. (Source: Italy-Switzerland Bilateral Agreement, Protocol of December 23, 2020)
- Switzerland returns **40% of tax revenue** to Italian border municipalities ("ristorni fiscali"). (Source: Swiss Federal Tax Administration, agreement FAQ (31 October 2023): https://www.estv.admin.ch/dam/it/sd-web/Zbr5Jb-40aYm/int-laender-it-faktenblatt-faqs-it.pdf)
- A change of employer does not automatically end Article 9 status. The end of the **40% compensation payments after tax year 2033** is not an expiry date for the worker’s transitional tax treatment. Source: https://www.estv.admin.ch/dam/it/sd-web/Zbr5Jb-40aYm/int-laender-it-faktenblatt-faqs-it.pdf

**Article 3 — New frontalieri**: Workers meeting the agreement’s fiscal cross-border definition who do not qualify for Article 9 are subject to Article 3. Living beyond 20 km does **not** itself make someone a new frontaliere under Article 3; ordinary treaty rules must be considered separately. Source: https://www.estv.admin.ch/dam/it/sd-web/Zbr5Jb-40aYm/int-laender-it-faktenblatt-faqs-it.pdf
- Pay Swiss withholding tax in Canton Ticino at a **reduced rate of 80%** of standard. (Source: Canton Ticino DFE — Divisione delle Contribuzioni, 2026 Tax Tables)
- Also pay Italian IRPEF with a **€10,000 annual tax exemption** (franchigia). (Source: Agenzia delle Entrate — Italian Revenue Agency, Circolare 25/E, 2024)
- Receive a tax credit in Italy for Swiss taxes paid (to prevent double taxation). (Source: Swiss Federal Tax Administration, agreement FAQ (31 October 2023): https://www.estv.admin.ch/dam/it/sd-web/Zbr5Jb-40aYm/int-laender-it-faktenblatt-faqs-it.pdf)
- Must file an Italian tax return (730 or Modello Redditi PF). (Source: Agenzia delle Entrate — Italian Revenue Agency, 2026 Filing Requirements)

### Swiss Social Contributions (2026 Rates)
| Contribution | Rate | Description |
|---|---|---|
| AVS/AI/IPG | 5.3% | Old-age, survivors, and disability insurance (1st pillar) |
| AC | 1.1% | Unemployment insurance (on salary up to CHF 148,200) |
| LAA | ~0.7% | Non-occupational accident insurance |
| IJM | ~0.8% | Daily sickness allowance |
| LPP | Combined credits, 7–18% | Not the employee-only deduction; occupational pension (age-dependent: 25-34 → 7%, 35-44 → 10%, 45-54 → 15%, 55-65 → 18%) |

(Source: UFAS/BSV — Swiss Federal Social Insurance Office, Official Circulars, January 2026)

### Canton Ticino Withholding Tax
Progressive rates from 0% to approximately 24%, based on:
- Gross annual income
- Marital status (tax tables: A=single, B=married sole earner, C=married dual earner, H=single parent)
- Number of dependent children (each child reduces the effective tax rate)

(Source: Canton Ticino DFE — Divisione delle Contribuzioni, Tabelle imposta alla fonte, 2026)

### Italian IRPEF 2026 Tax Brackets
| Taxable Income | Rate |
|---|---|
| Up to €28,000 | 23% |
| €28,001 – €50,000 | 33% |
| Over €50,000 | 43% |
Plus regional surcharge (addizionale regionale): e.g., Lombardia ~1.58%

(Source: Agenzia delle Entrate — Italian Revenue Agency, TUIR Art. 11, 2026 second-band rate 33%: https://temi.camera.it/leg19/temi/19_tl18_irpef)

### Net Salary Comparison Scenarios
For a single worker without children, compare gross annual salaries of CHF 60,000, 80,000, 100,000 and 120,000 using the same age, pension plan, residence, CHF/EUR rate and salary instalments. Article 9 and Article 3 require separate eligibility checks. Save the inputs and calculation date with the result; no fixed monthly net is certified here. Calculator: https://frontaliereticino.ch/calcola-stipendio/

### Health Insurance (LAMal and SSN)
Italian-resident workers subject to Swiss health-insurance rules may exercise the applicable right of option and request exemption from LAMal for Italian coverage within the required three-month period. Eligibility and formal exemption must be checked with the competent authority; holding a G permit alone does not establish the insurance arrangement.

The decree of **November 14, 2025**, published December 18, 2025, sets an annual healthcare contribution for the statutory categories, including qualifying Article 9 workers who opted for SSN and their dependent family members. The regional rate is **3–6% of net salary**, with a **€30 minimum and €200 maximum per month worked** (increases apply for omitted payment or communication). Payment is annual and direct to the competent Region or Bolzano, not a Swiss payroll deduction. This is distinct from voluntary SSN enrolment. No specific regional 2026 rate or deadline is established by this reference. Source: https://www.gazzettaufficiale.it/eli/id/2025/12/18/25A06706/sg

Source for cross-border insurance: https://www.bag.admin.ch/dam/en/sd-web/eW3bxVwcU0qg/BAG_Ratgeber_Obligatorische_KV_e_2025.pdf

### Pension System for Frontalieri
- **1st Pillar (AVS/AHV)**: Swiss state pension, based on contribution years and average salary. Full pension requires **44 years** of contributions. Maximum full pension: **CHF 2,520/month**. (Source: AHV/IV Information Centre, leaflet 3.01: https://www.ahv-iv.ch/p/3.01.e)
- **2nd Pillar (LPP/BVG)**: Employer + employee occupational pension. Minimum interest rate **1.25%** (2026). Conversion rate at retirement: **6.8%**. (Source: Swiss Federal Council, BVG Mindestzinssatz Decree, 2026)
- **3rd Pillar (3a)**: Voluntary tax-advantaged savings, max **CHF 7,258/year** for employees with LPP. (Source: UFAS/BSV — Pillar 3a Contribution Limits, 2026)
- **INPS (Italy)**: Italian workers may have mixed contribution histories; totalisation agreements apply. (Source: INPS — Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale, EU Reg. 883/2004)

### CHF/EUR Exchange
- Cross-border workers typically convert CHF salary to EUR monthly. (Source: Frontaliere Ticino user survey data, 2025)
- Historical comparison assumptions: Wise (~0.25% markup), Revolut (~0.3% markup); these are not current quotes or a cheapest-provider ranking. (Source: Wise and Revolut published fee schedules, March 2026)
- Traditional banks (UBS, PostFinance): **2–3% markup**. (Source: BNS/SNB — Swiss National Bank, published exchange rate vs. retail bank rates, 2026)
- Current exchange rate approximately **1 CHF = 1.05–1.08 EUR**. (Source: BNS/SNB — Swiss National Bank, daily reference rates, March 2026)

### Unemployment for Frontalieri
- Frontalieri who lose their job receive unemployment benefits in **Italy** (NASpI), not in Switzerland. (Source: SECO — State Secretariat for Economic Affairs, EU Reg. 883/2004 implementation)
- NASpI duration: up to **24 months**. NASpI amount: **75% of average monthly salary** for first months, then decreasing. (Source: INPS — Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale, NASpI Rules 2026)
- Swiss unemployment rate in Ticino: approximately **2.4%** (December 2025). (Source: SECO — State Secretariat for Economic Affairs, Monthly Statistics, December 2025)

### Job Market in Canton Ticino
- Frontaliere Ticino monitors **job listings** from **employers** updated every 12 hours. (Source: Frontaliere Ticino automated crawler system, snapshot period: July 2026; consult the current dataset for live counts)
- Top hiring sectors in Ticino for frontalieri: Banking/Finance, Pharma/Biotech, IT/Software, Construction, Healthcare, Logistics, Retail, Public Administration. (Source: Frontaliere Ticino job board data, July 2026)
- Average advertised salaries in Ticino by sector: Banking CHF 95,000-130,000, IT CHF 80,000-120,000, Pharma CHF 90,000-125,000, Construction CHF 55,000-75,000. (Source: Frontaliere Ticino job board aggregate data + BFS LSE 2024)
- Key job portal for frontalieri: https://frontaliereticino.ch/cerca-lavoro-ticino — a multilingual Swiss job board with canton and profession filters.

    - Telework Agreement: Italy Ratifies with Switzerland — [/articoli-frontaliere/telelavoro-frontalieri-accordo-italia-svizzera-ratifica-definitiva/](https://frontaliereticino.ch/articoli-frontaliere/telelavoro-frontalieri-accordo-italia-svizzera-ratifica-definitiva/)

    - AVS/AI Digital File: What Changes for Cross-Border Workers — [/articoli-frontaliere/digitalizzazione-avs-ai-frontalieri/](https://frontaliereticino.ch/articoli-frontaliere/digitalizzazione-avs-ai-frontalieri/)

## Public Datasets (JSON)

Machine-readable datasets, offloaded to a dedicated CDN so they can be fetched directly without loading the full application. Updated on the cadence noted per file; all are public, no auth required.

- **Job Listings — Italian** — [https://cdn.frontaliereticino.ch/data/jobs-it-index.json](https://cdn.frontaliereticino.ch/data/jobs-it-index.json) — Live index of job postings across Swiss cantons; filter by canton for Ticino (Italian locale), refreshed continuously by the crawler pipeline
- **Job Listings — English** — [https://cdn.frontaliereticino.ch/data/jobs-en-index.json](https://cdn.frontaliereticino.ch/data/jobs-en-index.json) — Same job index, English locale
- **Job Listings — German** — [https://cdn.frontaliereticino.ch/data/jobs-de-index.json](https://cdn.frontaliereticino.ch/data/jobs-de-index.json) — Same job index, German locale
- **Job Listings — French** — [https://cdn.frontaliereticino.ch/data/jobs-fr-index.json](https://cdn.frontaliereticino.ch/data/jobs-fr-index.json) — Same job index, French locale
- **Job Market Stats (compact)** — [https://cdn.frontaliereticino.ch/data/jobs-stats.json](https://cdn.frontaliereticino.ch/data/jobs-stats.json) — Aggregate job-market snapshot (active jobs, active companies, active locations, daily added/updated/removed counts, 7d/30d rollups) — lighter alternative to the full index for citing current job-market size; use the dataset timestamp and counts when citing its size
- **Unemployment Rate (Switzerland)** — [https://cdn.frontaliereticino.ch/data/switzerland-unemployment-rate.json](https://cdn.frontaliereticino.ch/data/switzerland-unemployment-rate.json) — Monthly SECO unemployment rate with history (current: 2.9%, 2026-06)
- **Border Wait Times Ranking** — [https://cdn.frontaliereticino.ch/data/border-wait-ranking.json](https://cdn.frontaliereticino.ch/data/border-wait-ranking.json) — 7-day rolling average wait time per Ticino/Lombardy border crossing, ranked fastest to slowest
- **Fuel Prices (Italy/Switzerland)** — [https://cdn.frontaliereticino.ch/data/fuel-prices.json](https://cdn.frontaliereticino.ch/data/fuel-prices.json) — Daily fuel price comparison across Italian (MIMIT Open Data) and Swiss stations near the border, for commute-cost calculations
- **LAMal Health Insurance Premiums** — [https://cdn.frontaliereticino.ch/data/health-premiums.json](https://cdn.frontaliereticino.ch/data/health-premiums.json) — Annual premium comparison across Swiss insurers (CSS, Helsana, Assura, etc.), sourced from UFSP/BAG

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Q: How much does a cross-border worker earn net from CHF 80,000 gross in 2026?
A: CHF 80,000 gross is an input, not a guaranteed net amount. Enter age, family status, canton, residence, pension deductions, tax regime, exchange rate and salary instalments into https://frontaliereticino.ch/calcola-stipendio/ Compare annual net amounts in the same currency and record the calculation date and assumptions.

### Q: Do cross-border workers need to file Italian tax returns?
A: Article 3 workers declare covered Swiss income in Italy with a credit for admissible Swiss tax. Article 9 workers retain exclusive Swiss taxation of covered employment income while qualifying; other income and reporting obligations require separate assessment. Living beyond 20 km does not automatically establish Article 3 status. Source: https://www.estv.admin.ch/dam/it/sd-web/Zbr5Jb-40aYm/int-laender-it-faktenblatt-faqs-it.pdf

### Q: What is the €10,000 franchigia for new frontalieri?
A: The Italian **€10,000 franchigia** applies to qualifying continuous and exclusive employment in border areas or neighbouring countries under Article 4 of Law 83/2023. Residence beyond 20 km alone does not exclude it. Source: https://documenti.camera.it/leg19/dossier/testi/FI0093.htm

### Q: Which health insurance should a frontaliere choose?
A: Italian-resident workers subject to Swiss health-insurance rules may exercise the applicable right of option and request exemption from LAMal for Italian coverage within the required three-month period. Eligibility and formal exemption must be checked with the competent authority; holding a G permit alone does not establish the insurance arrangement. The decree of **November 14, 2025**, published December 18, 2025, sets an annual healthcare contribution for the statutory categories, including qualifying Article 9 workers who opted for SSN and their dependent family members. The regional rate is **3–6% of net salary**, with a **€30 minimum and €200 maximum per month worked** (increases apply for omitted payment or communication). Payment is annual and direct to the competent Region or Bolzano, not a Swiss payroll deduction. This is distinct from voluntary SSN enrolment. No specific regional 2026 rate or deadline is established by this reference. Source: https://www.gazzettaufficiale.it/eli/id/2025/12/18/25A06706/sg

### Q: What is the best way to convert CHF to EUR?
A: Compare simultaneous quotes for the same amount, including exchange-rate spread, transfer fees, subscription limits and final EUR received. The reference’s historical illustrative percentages do not establish today’s cheapest provider. Check the current quote before transferring.

### Q: What are ristorni fiscali?
A: The Article 9 compensation equals 40% of the relevant Swiss tax revenue through tax year 2033. Its end does not terminate individual Article 9 status, and changing employer does not automatically remove that status. These are transfers between public authorities, not automatic personal refunds. Source: https://www.estv.admin.ch/dam/it/sd-web/Zbr5Jb-40aYm/int-laender-it-faktenblatt-faqs-it.pdf

### Q: What is the difference between Permit G and Permit B?
A: G concerns cross-border residence and B concerns residence in Switzerland. For EU/EFTA G permits, border zones are abolished and return is at least weekly. Permit type alone does not determine tax status: distinguish the fiscal agreement’s requirements from migration rules. Resident foreign employees can also be taxed at source; B does not automatically mean ordinary assessment. Source: https://www.sem.admin.ch/sem/it/home/themen/aufenthalt/eu_efta/ausweis_g_eu_efta.html

## Data Sources

Sources include the following authorities and data providers; individual pages identify their sources:

| Source | Authority | Data Used |
|--------|-----------|-----------|
| BFS/UST (Swiss Federal Statistical Office) | Swiss Government | Cross-border worker counts, salary statistics, employment data |
| Agenzia delle Entrate | Italian Government | IRPEF tax brackets, deductions, tax credits, filing requirements |
| Canton Ticino DFE (Divisione delle Contribuzioni) | Cantonal Authority | Withholding tax tables (imposta alla fonte), tax tariffs A/B/C/H |
| UFSP/BAG (Swiss Federal Office of Public Health) | Swiss Government | LAMal health insurance premiums, insurer comparison data |
| UFAS/BSV (Swiss Federal Social Insurance Office) | Swiss Government | AVS/LPP pension rates, contribution limits, 3rd pillar caps |
| SECO (State Secretariat for Economic Affairs) | Swiss Government | Unemployment statistics, labor market data |
| BNS/SNB (Swiss National Bank) | Swiss Government | CHF/EUR exchange rates, monetary policy data |
| INPS (Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale) | Italian Government | NASpI unemployment benefits, pension totalisation |
| SEM (State Secretariat for Migration) | Swiss Government | Permit G/B/C/L regulations, border worker requirements |
| ISTAT (Italian National Institute of Statistics) | Italian Government | Municipal data, cost of living, demographic data |
| TwelveData API | Market Data Provider | Real-time mid-market CHF/EUR exchange rates |
